events.title: Early Arabian Civilizations
events.description: Early settlements and trade routes emerged on the Arabian Peninsula. The Dilmun civilization (present-day Bahrain region) traded with Mesopotamia. Arabia became a crucial hub connecting East-West trade, with spices, frankincense, and myrrh transported through here to the Mediterranean world.

events.title: Rise of the Kingdom of Sheba
events.description: The legendary Kingdom of Sheba rose in southern Arabia (present-day Yemen region). The Queen of Sheba reportedly visited King Solomon. This kingdom controlled frankincense trade routes, becoming a prosperous commercial civilization.

events.title: Nabataeans Establish Trade Network
events.description: The Nabataeans established an extensive trade network in northwestern Arabia, controlling caravan routes from Arabia Felix to the Mediterranean. Their capital Petra became a crucial trading hub. Nabataeans mastered desert water management, creating an oasis civilization.

events.title: Formation of Arab Tribes
events.description: Arab tribes formed in the Arabian Peninsula, primarily nomadic Bedouins. These tribes developed unique survival skills and cultural traditions. Tribal system became the foundation of Arabian society, influencing later Islamic civilization.

events.title: Red Sea Trade Flourishes
events.description: Red Sea trade routes flourished, connecting Arabia with the Roman Empire, India, and East Africa. Arabian ports like Jeddah became important commercial centers. Spices, silk, precious stones, and slaves were transported through Arabia, bringing wealth.

events.title: Birth of Prophet Muhammad
events.description: The Prophet Muhammad was born in Mecca to the Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. His birth marked the beginning of one of the most significant religious movements in human history.

events.title: Muhammad's First Revelation
events.description: While meditating in the Cave of Hira, Muhammad received his first revelation from the Angel Gabriel. This marked the beginning of the Quranic revelations and the birth of Islam. Muhammad began secretly spreading monotheistic faith in Mecca.

events.title: Public Preaching Begins
events.description: Muhammad began publicly preaching Islam in Mecca, calling for monotheism and social justice. Meccan elites resisted, fearing threats to their economic interests and traditional beliefs. Early Muslims faced persecution, some migrating to Abyssinia for refuge.

events.title: The Hijra (Migration)
events.description: Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Yathrib (later renamed Medina). This migration marks the starting point of the Islamic calendar. In Medina, Muhammad established the first Islamic political community and drafted the Constitution of Medina.

events.title: Battle of Badr
events.description: Muslims achieved their first major military victory against the Meccans at Badr. Though outnumbered, Muslim forces defeated the Meccan army, boosting morale. This victory was seen as divine intervention, consolidating Muhammad's position.

events.title: Battle of Uhud
events.description: Meccans sought revenge at Uhud, initially defeating Muslims. Muhammad was wounded; many Muslims died. This setback taught the importance of discipline and obedience. Despite defeat, Muslims maintained control of Medina.

events.title: Battle of the Trench
events.description: Meccans and allies besieged Medina with 10,000 troops. Muslims dug defensive trenches, a novel tactic. The siege lasted two weeks; coalition forces withdrew due to weather and internal discord. This victory secured Medina's position.

events.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
events.description: Muhammad and Meccans signed a ten-year peace treaty at Hudaybiyyah. Though controversial among Muslims, the treaty brought peace and allowed Islam to spread. Many tribes converted during this period.

events.title: Battle of Mu'tah
events.description: Muslim forces fought the Byzantine Empire at Mu'tah (in present-day Jordan), the first confrontation with a major power. Though Muslims retreated, the battle demonstrated Islamic expansion beyond Arabia. This marked the beginning of Muslim-Byzantine conflicts.

events.title: Conquest of Mecca
events.description: Muhammad led ten thousand Muslims in a peaceful conquest of Mecca. He pardoned most Meccans, destroyed idols around the Kaaba, and converted it into an Islamic holy site. The conquest of Mecca marked Islam's triumph in the Arabian Peninsula.

events.title: Farewell Pilgrimage
events.description: Muhammad performed his first and only Hajj pilgrimage after conquering Mecca, accompanied by thousands of Muslims. He delivered the Farewell Sermon at Mount Arafat, summarizing Islamic teachings and emphasizing equality and justice. This pilgrimage established Hajj rituals.

events.title: Death of Prophet Muhammad
events.description: Muhammad died in Medina at age 63. His death triggered a succession crisis in the Muslim community. Abu Bakr was chosen as the first Caliph (successor), beginning the Rashidun Caliphate period.

events.title: Caliphate of Abu Bakr
events.description: Abu Bakr, Muhammad's closest companion, became the first Caliph. He suppressed the Ridda Wars (apostasy wars), reunifying the Arabian Peninsula under Islam. Abu Bakr initiated Muslim conquests of Syria and Iraq, laying foundations for Islamic expansion.

events.title: Caliphate of Umar
events.description: Umar ibn al-Khattab's caliphate saw the most dramatic Islamic expansion. Muslim armies conquered Syria, Palestine, Egypt, Iraq, and Persia. Umar established administrative systems and Islamic calendar. He was assassinated in 644 by a Persian slave.

events.title: Caliphate of Uthman
events.description: Uthman ibn Affan's caliphate continued expansion but faced internal strife. He compiled the Quran into a standardized text. Opposition to his nepotism grew; Egyptian rebels assassinated him in Medina, triggering the First Fitna (civil war).

events.title: Caliphate of Ali and Civil War
events.description: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, became the fourth Caliph. He faced opposition from Muawiyah and Aisha, leading to battles at Camel and Siffin. The Muslim community split into Sunni and Shi'a. Ali was assassinated in 661; Muawiyah established the Umayyad Caliphate.

events.title: Umayyad Caliphate Established
events.description: Muawiyah I founded the Umayyad Caliphate, making Damascus the capital. The Umayyads transformed the caliphate into a hereditary monarchy. Under Umayyad rule, the Islamic empire expanded from Spain to India, though Arabia's political importance declined.

events.title: Tragedy of Karbala
events.description: Hussein ibn Ali, Muhammad's grandson, was killed at Karbala (Iraq) by Umayyad forces. His martyrdom became central to Shi'a Islam, commemorated annually as Ashura. This event deepened the Sunni-Shi'a divide.

events.title: Abbasid Revolution
events.description: The Abbasid Revolution overthrew the Umayyad Caliphate. The Abbasids moved the capital to Baghdad. Though politically marginalized, Mecca and Medina retained religious significance as Islam's holiest cities. The Hajj pilgrimage remained a crucial annual event.

events.title: Hajj Trade Flourishes
events.description: Annual Hajj pilgrimage brought economic prosperity to the Hejaz region. Pilgrims from across the Muslim world converged on Mecca, stimulating trade and cultural exchange. Local rulers profited from providing services to pilgrims.

events.title: Qarmatian Attack on Mecca
events.description: The radical Qarmatian sect attacked Mecca during Hajj, massacring pilgrims and stealing the Black Stone from the Kaaba. The stone was returned 21 years later. This attack shocked the Muslim world and disrupted the Hajj for years.

events.title: Sharifs of Mecca Rule
events.description: The Sharifs, descendants of Muhammad, ruled Mecca and the Hejaz region. They managed holy sites and Hajj logistics. The Sharifs maintained autonomy while nominally recognizing various caliphates and empires.

events.title: Mongol Destruction of Abbasid Caliphate
events.description: Mongols sacked Baghdad and killed the Abbasid Caliph, ending the caliphate. Though Arabia wasn't directly invaded, the political vacuum affected the region. The Mamluks of Egypt emerged as protectors of the holy cities.

events.title: Mamluk Control of Hejaz
events.description: The Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt established control over the Hejaz, including Mecca and Medina. Mamluks protected pilgrimage routes and maintained order in holy cities. Their rule lasted until Ottoman conquest.

events.title: Timurid Threat
events.description: Timur (Tamerlane) threatened Arabia during his conquests but didn't invade. His devastation of surrounding regions disrupted trade and pilgrimage routes. Arabia remained relatively isolated during this period.

events.title: Ottoman Conquest
events.description: The Ottoman Empire defeated the Mamluks and took control of the Hejaz. Ottomans claimed the title of 'Protector of the Two Holy Mosques.' Ottoman rule brought stability but also centralized control. The Sharifs continued governing Mecca under Ottoman suzerainty.

events.title: First Saudi State Founded
events.description: Muhammad ibn Saud allied with religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, establishing the Saudi state in Najd. They promoted strict Wahhabi doctrine, opposing saint worship and religious innovation.

events.title: Saudi Conquest of Mecca and Medina
events.description: The First Saudi State, under Abdulaziz ibn Saud and his son Saud, conquered the Hejaz including Mecca and Medina. They destroyed tombs and shrines, deeming them heretical worship. This alarmed the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Egyptian-Ottoman Campaign
events.description: The Ottoman Sultan ordered Egyptian Governor Muhammad Ali to attack the Saudi state. After years of war, Egyptian forces captured Diriyah (Saudi capital); the First Saudi State fell. Saudi leaders were sent to Constantinople for execution.

events.title: Second Saudi State Founded
events.description: Turki ibn Abdullah re-established the Saudi state with Riyadh as capital. The Second Saudi State reunified Najd but failed to recover the Hejaz. This state lasted until the late 19th century.

events.title: Reign of Faisal ibn Turki
events.description: Faisal ibn Turki became the most successful ruler of the Second Saudi State. He expanded territory, strengthened centralization, and promoted trade and agriculture. His reign represented the golden age of the Second Saudi State.

events.title: Rashidi Conquest of Riyadh
events.description: The Rashidi family of Hail conquered Riyadh; the Second Saudi State fell. The Saud family fled to Kuwait. Young Abdulaziz ibn Saud (Ibn Saud) spent his childhood in Kuwaiti exile.

events.title: Ibn Saud's Raid on Riyadh
events.description: 22-year-old Abdulaziz ibn Saud led a small force in a daring raid to recapture Riyadh, retaking his ancestral city. This bold attack marked the beginning of the Third Saudi State and modern Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Conquest of Al-Hasa
events.description: Ibn Saud seized the Al-Hasa region (Eastern Province) from the Ottoman Empire. This victory gave the Saudis control of the Arabian Gulf coast and important economic resources.

events.title: Treaty of Darin
events.description: Ibn Saud signed the Treaty of Darin with Britain, gaining British recognition and support. Britain recognized Najd and Al-Hasa as Saudi territory; Ibn Saud promised WWI neutrality and to oppose the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Conquest of Hejaz Begins
events.description: Ibn Saud launched an offensive against the Hejaz, challenging King Hussein of the Hashemite family. Ikhwan (religious warriors) forces captured Taif. King Hussein abdicated, succeeded by his son Ali.

events.title: Conquest of Mecca and Medina
events.description: Ibn Saud completely conquered the Hejaz, entering Mecca and Medina. King Ali fled to Iraq. Ibn Saud became King of Hejaz and Sultan of Najd, unifying most of the Arabian Peninsula.

events.title: Ibn Saud Crowned King of Hejaz
events.description: Ibn Saud was formally crowned King of Hejaz in Mecca. He convened a pan-Islamic conference, seeking Muslim world recognition as guardian of holy sites. Most Islamic countries eventually recognized his rule.

events.title: Treaty of Jeddah
events.description: Britain recognized Ibn Saud's sovereignty in the Treaty of Jeddah, replacing the Darin Treaty. Britain acknowledged the independence of the Hejaz and Najd kingdoms. This marked international recognition of Saudi power.

events.title: Ikhwan Rebellion Suppressed
events.description: The Ikhwan religious warriors rebelled against Ibn Saud, opposing his modernization policies and diplomacy with infidels. Ibn Saud suppressed the rebellion, consolidating his power. This ended the Ikhwan's influence in Saudi politics.

events.title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Established
events.description: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud unified the Hejaz and Najd into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. He became the first king, founding the Saudi dynasty. September 23 became Saudi National Day, still celebrated today.

events.title: Agreement with Standard Oil
events.description: The Saudi government signed an oil exploration concession agreement with Standard Oil Company of California (later Aramco). This agreement changed Saudi Arabia's destiny, laying the foundation for future oil wealth.

events.title: Oil Discovered
events.description: Commercial quantities of oil were discovered at Dammam Well No. 7 near Dhahran. This discovery proved Saudi Arabia possessed one of the world's richest oil reserves. Saudi Arabia transformed from an impoverished desert kingdom into a future oil giant.

events.title: Ibn Saud Meets Roosevelt
events.description: At WWII's end, King Ibn Saud met US President Roosevelt aboard the USS Quincy in the Suez Canal. This historic meeting laid the foundation for the US-Saudi special relationship: oil in exchange for security guarantees.

events.title: Joins Arab League
events.description: Saudi Arabia became a founding member of the Arab League. As guardian of Islam's holy sites, Saudi Arabia enjoyed special status in the Arab and Islamic worlds.

events.title: Joins United Nations
events.description: Saudi Arabia became a founding member of the United Nations, participating in the San Francisco Conference. Though a small country, oil resources and holy site guardianship gave Saudi Arabia international importance.

events.title: First Arab-Israeli War
events.description: Saudi Arabia joined Arab forces against the newly established Israel. Though military contributions were limited, Saudi Arabia provided financial support. Israel's establishment became a core issue in Saudi foreign policy.

events.title: Death of Ibn Saud
events.description: Founding King Abdulaziz Ibn Saud died aged 77. He ruled Saudi Arabia for over 50 years, building a modern state from a desert chieftain. His son Saud succeeded as king.

events.title: Reign of King Saud
events.description: During King Saud's reign, oil revenues grew dramatically, but his lavish lifestyle and ineffective management caused financial difficulties. Royal family doubts about his competence eventually led to his deposition.

events.title: Stance During Suez Crisis
events.description: During the Suez Crisis, Saudi Arabia supported Egyptian President Nasser against Anglo-French-Israeli aggression. But Saudi Arabia had ideological differences with Nasser's Arab nationalism, fearing its threat to monarchy.

events.title: OPEC Founded
events.description: Saudi Arabia co-founded the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) with Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, and Venezuela. OPEC's establishment enabled producer countries to control oil production and pricing, transforming the global oil market landscape.

events.title: Yemen Civil War Intervention
events.description: Saudi Arabia supported Yemeni royalists against Egyptian-backed republicans. This proxy war consumed substantial Saudi resources, but republicans ultimately won. This highlighted Saudi Arabia's ideological confrontation with Nasser's Arab socialism.

events.title: King Faisal Ascends
events.description: Crown Prince Faisal launched a bloodless coup, deposing his brother King Saud. After ruling as regent for years, Faisal formally became king. He implemented fiscal reforms and modernization policies, becoming one of Saudi Arabia's most respected monarchs.

events.title: Six-Day War
events.description: In the Six-Day War, Israel defeated Arab forces. Saudi Arabia provided financial support and briefly embargoed oil to the West. The war's outcome intensified the Arab-Israeli conflict; Saudi Arabia pledged support for the Palestinian cause.

events.title: Organization of Islamic Cooperation Founded
events.description: After the Al-Aqsa Mosque arson, King Faisal initiated the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), headquartered in Jeddah. This made Saudi Arabia the political leader of the Islamic world, not just a religious center.

events.title: First Five-Year Development Plan
events.description: Saudi Arabia launched its first five-year development plan, using oil revenues to build infrastructure, education, healthcare, and industry. This marked the beginning of systematic modernization, transforming Saudi Arabia from tribal society to modern state.

events.title: Oil Embargo and Price Surge
events.description: During the Yom Kippur War, Saudi Arabia led Arab oil producers in an embargo against Western countries supporting Israel. Oil prices soared from $3 to $12 per barrel. The oil weapon demonstrated Saudi Arabia's global influence, bringing enormous wealth.

events.title: Assassination of King Faisal
events.description: King Faisal was assassinated by his nephew Faisal bin Musaid, shocking the nation and Islamic world. The assassin acted from personal grudges rather than political motives. Faisal's half-brother Prince Khalid succeeded as king.

events.title: Reign of King Khalid
events.description: During King Khalid's reign, Saudi Arabia experienced oil prosperity. Massive infrastructure construction transformed the nation. Crown Prince Fahd handled day-to-day governance. Khalid was respected for his piety and humility.

events.title: Grand Mosque Seizure
events.description: Extremist Juhayman al-Otaybi and his followers seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca, proclaiming the Mahdi's arrival. After a two-week bloody siege, Saudi forces (with French special forces assistance) retook the mosque. This incident shocked the Islamic world and exposed Saudi security vulnerabilities.

events.title: Impact of Iranian Islamic Revolution
events.description: Iran's Pahlavi Dynasty was overthrown, establishing the Islamic Republic. Khomeini's Shi'a revolutionary ideology threatened Saudi Arabia's Sunni monarchy. Saudi-Iranian geopolitical competition began, becoming the Middle East's major fault line.

events.title: Supporting Iraq During Iran-Iraq War
events.description: During the Iran-Iraq War, Saudi Arabia provided tens of billions of dollars in aid to Iraq, countering Iranian Shi'a expansion. Saudi Arabia feared Khomeini's revolution export to the Gulf region. This war deepened Saudi-Iranian hostility.

events.title: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Founded
events.description: Saudi Arabia, with Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman, established the Gulf Cooperation Council to address the Iranian threat. The GCC promoted economic integration and security cooperation, making Saudi Arabia the indisputable Gulf leader.

events.title: King Fahd Ascends
events.description: After King Khalid's death, Crown Prince Fahd succeeded. Fahd adopted the title 'Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques' instead of 'Majesty,' emphasizing religious legitimacy. He ruled for 25 years, witnessing oil prosperity and challenges.

events.title: Support for Afghan Mujahideen
events.description: Saudi Arabia provided billions of dollars to Afghan mujahideen resisting Soviet invasion, matching US aid. Thousands of Saudi volunteers (including Osama bin Laden) joined jihad. This support cultivated extremist forces that later turned against Saudi Arabia and the West.

events.title: Oil Price Crash
events.description: International oil prices crashed from $30/barrel in 1985 to below $10/barrel in 1986. This oil price collapse ended the oil boom era; Saudi Arabia was forced to cut spending, adjust economic policies, and promote economic diversification.

events.title: Hajj Tragedy in Mecca
events.description: Iranian pilgrims held political demonstrations during Hajj; clashes with Saudi security killed over 400. This incident further deteriorated Saudi-Iranian relations. Saudi Arabia accused Iran of politicizing the Hajj.

events.title: Iraqi Invasion of Kuwait
events.description: Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait; Saddam Hussein's forces amassed at the Saudi border. Facing direct military threat, King Fahd made the difficult decision to allow foreign troops to be stationed.

events.title: Gulf War
events.description: Saudi Arabia allowed over 500,000 US-led coalition forces to be stationed, becoming the base for liberating Kuwait. The stationing of non-Muslim troops in the holy land sparked strong opposition from religious conservatives. The Gulf War established close US-Saudi military alliance but also planted seeds of Bin Laden's extremism.

events.title: Basic Law Promulgated
events.description: King Fahd promulgated the Basic Law (effectively a constitution), formally establishing Saudi Arabia as an Islamic monarchy with the Quran and Sunnah as constitution. The Basic Law stipulated royal succession among Ibn Saud's sons and grandsons.

events.title: King Fahd's Stroke
events.description: King Fahd suffered a severe stroke; his health deteriorated. Crown Prince Abdullah began actual regency. Fahd nominally retained the kingship until his death in 2005, but Abdullah held real power.

events.title: Khobar Towers Bombing
events.description: The Khobar Towers US military complex near Dhahran in the Eastern Province was attacked by truck bomb; 19 US soldiers died. This attack revealed the terrorist threat facing Saudi Arabia, possibly linked to Bin Laden's Al-Qaeda or Iranian-backed Shi'a radicals.

events.title: Bin Laden Issues Jihad Declaration
events.description: Saudi dissident Osama bin Laden, exiled in Afghanistan, issued the 'Declaration of Jihad Against the Americans Occupying the Land of the Two Holy Mosques.' He condemned US troops stationed in Saudi Arabia and called for overthrowing the Saudi royal family. Bin Laden became public enemy number one for Saudi Arabia and the US.

events.title: Oil Prices Crash Again
events.description: The Asian financial crisis caused oil demand to decline; prices fell below $10/barrel, the lowest in 25 years. Saudi Arabia led OPEC in cutting production to support prices. Economic difficulties sparked calls for social reform.

events.title: 9/11 Attacks
events.description: Al-Qaeda launched 9/11 attacks on the US; 15 of 19 hijackers were Saudi citizens. This fact shocked the world, Saudi Arabia faced international pressure, questioned about its role in fostering extremism. US-Saudi relations entered crisis.

events.title: Riyadh Bombings
events.description: Al-Qaeda launched coordinated terrorist attacks on residential compounds in Riyadh, killing 39. This marked the beginning of a wave of terrorism targeting Saudi Arabia itself. The government launched a massive counter-terrorism campaign.

events.title: War on Terror
events.description: Saudi Arabia experienced a series of terrorist attacks as Al-Qaeda attempted to overthrow the royal family. The government conducted fierce crackdowns, killing or arresting most terrorists. Saudi Arabia strengthened intelligence cooperation with the US while implementing deradicalization programs.

events.title: King Abdullah Formally Ascends
events.description: After King Fahd's death, Abdullah, who had been regent for 10 years, formally became king. Abdullah was seen as a moderate reformer, promising gradual modernization. He appointed Prince Sultan as Crown Prince and Prince Nayef as Second Deputy Prime Minister.

events.title: First Municipal Elections
events.description: Saudi Arabia held its first national municipal elections, allowing male voters to elect half of city council members. Though limited in power and excluding women, this was seen as a small step forward in political reform.

events.title: Joins World Trade Organization
events.description: After 12 years of negotiations, Saudi Arabia officially joined the World Trade Organization (WTO). WTO membership required Saudi Arabia to open its economy, lower tariffs, and reform business laws, seen as an important step in economic modernization.

events.title: KAUST Opens
events.description: The $10 billion King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) opened, Saudi Arabia's first co-educational university. KAUST symbolized Saudi Arabia's commitment to scientific research and educational modernization, but also drew conservative criticism.

events.title: Response to Arab Spring
events.description: Facing the Arab Spring sweeping the Middle East, King Abdullah announced a $130 billion welfare spending package, including housing, salary increases, and unemployment benefits, to quell any discontent. Saudi Arabia also sent troops into Bahrain to suppress Shi'a protests.

events.title: Women Granted Voting Rights
events.description: King Abdullah announced that women would gain the right to vote and run in the 2015 municipal elections. This was a historic breakthrough for Saudi women's rights, though still far from enough.

events.title: Women Appointed to Shura Council
events.description: King Abdullah appointed 30 women to the 150-member Shura (Consultative) Council, allowing women to participate in the legislative process for the first time. Women comprised 20% of council seats, exceeding many Western countries.

events.title: King Salman Ascends
events.description: King Abdullah died at age 90. His half-brother Prince Salman ascended at age 79. Salman quickly reorganized government, appointing his son Mohammed bin Salman as Defense Minister and Deputy Crown Prince, opening a new era.

events.title: Yemen War Intervention
events.description: Saudi Arabia led an Arab coalition in military operations against Yemen's Houthi forces. King Salman and 31-year-old Defense Minister Prince Mohammed viewed the operation as countering Iranian expansion. The Yemen war became a costly quagmire, causing a humanitarian disaster.

events.title: Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition Formed
events.description: Saudi Arabia announced the formation of a 34-nation Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition, headquartered in Riyadh. This coalition aimed to coordinate anti-terrorism efforts and demonstrate Saudi leadership in the Islamic world.

events.title: Vision 2030 Announced
events.description: Deputy Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman unveiled the ambitious Vision 2030, planning to diversify Saudi economy and reduce oil dependence. Plans include privatization, developing tourism and entertainment industries, and increasing female labor participation.

events.title: Saudi Aramco IPO Plan
events.description: As part of Vision 2030, the government announced plans to list 5% of state oil company Saudi Aramco. This would be history's largest IPO. The plan demonstrated Saudi Arabia's serious commitment to economic transformation.

events.title: Mohammed bin Salman Becomes Crown Prince
events.description: King Salman deposed Crown Prince Mohammed bin Nayef, appointing his son Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) as Crown Prince. This surprising move consolidated MBS's position as de facto ruler, despite being only 31.

events.title: Qatar Diplomatic Crisis
events.description: Saudi Arabia, with UAE, Bahrain, and Egypt, imposed a comprehensive blockade on Qatar, accusing it of supporting terrorism and being close to Iran. This unprecedented Gulf crisis lasted three and a half years, highlighting GCC divisions.

events.title: Women's Driving Ban Lifted
events.description: King Salman issued a decree allowing women to drive, ending the world's only women's driving ban. This decision took effect in June 2018, seen as a landmark reform of MBS's modernization agenda.

events.title: Anti-Corruption Crackdown
events.description: MBS launched a massive anti-corruption campaign, detaining hundreds of princes, ministers, and businessmen at the Ritz-Carlton in Riyadh. The government claimed to recover over $100 billion. Critics saw it as power consolidation and purging dissenters.

events.title: Women Permitted to Drive
events.description: Women officially gained the right to drive in Saudi Arabia. Thousands of women celebrated this historic moment. Though major progress, women's rights activists were simultaneously arrested, drawing international criticism.

events.title: Khashoggi Murder
events.description: Saudi dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi was murdered and dismembered in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. This brutal act shocked the world, severely damaging MBS's international reputation. Despite Saudi denials, MBS is widely believed to have ordered the murder.

events.title: Aramco Oil Facilities Attacked
events.description: Two key Saudi Aramco oil facilities were attacked by drones and cruise missiles, cutting 5% of global oil supply. Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility, but the US and Saudi Arabia blamed Iranian backing. The attack exposed Saudi energy infrastructure vulnerability.

events.title: Saudi Aramco Successfully Listed
events.description: Saudi Aramco listed on the Riyadh Stock Exchange, raising $25.6 billion in history's largest IPO. Aramco was valued at $1.7 trillion, becoming the world's most valuable company. The listing was a key Vision 2030 milestone.

events.title: Oil Price War and COVID-19 Pandemic
events.description: Saudi-Russia production cut negotiations broke down, triggering an oil price war. Combined with COVID-19 demand shock, oil prices crashed to historic lows, even negative prices. Saudi economy suffered a double blow, forced to cut spending and increase VAT.

events.title: Death Penalty Restrictions Eased
events.description: Saudi Arabia announced restrictions on death penalty for minors (under 18 at time of crime), replacing it with maximum 10 years in juvenile detention. This reform was seen as part of MBS's human rights image improvement efforts.

events.title: Gulf Crisis Ends
events.description: At the Al-Ula Summit, Saudi Arabia and Qatar agreed to restore diplomatic relations, ending the three-and-a-half-year blockade. This reconciliation reflected Saudi foreign policy pragmatism and desire to present a united front against Iran.

events.title: NEOM Megacity Construction
events.description: Saudi Arabia accelerated construction of the NEOM megacity project, a $500 billion futuristic metropolis on the Red Sea coast. NEOM includes concepts like The Line linear city, symbolizing Saudi commitment to technology and sustainability as a post-oil future.

events.title: Dialogue with Iran Resumes
events.description: Mediated by Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Iran began secret talks, seeking to ease tensions. Dialogue focused on Yemen conflict and regional security. This marked a pragmatic shift in Saudi foreign policy.

events.title: LIV Golf Series Launched
events.description: The Saudi Public Investment Fund-backed LIV Golf Series launched, challenging traditional PGA Tour. Massive prize money attracted top players. This was part of Saudi sports washing strategy, but drew human rights criticism.

events.title: Biden Visits Saudi Arabia
events.description: US President Biden visited Saudi Arabia, meeting with MBS. Despite Biden's promise to make Saudi Arabia a 'pariah,' high oil prices and geopolitical realities forced reconciliation. The visit highlighted the complexity and interdependence of US-Saudi relations.

events.title: OPEC+ Production Cut Decision
events.description: Under Saudi leadership, OPEC+ decided to cut production by 2 million barrels per day, pushing up oil prices. This decision defied US wishes for increased production to lower prices, seen as a signal of Saudi's more independent foreign policy and overture to Russia.

events.title: Diplomatic Relations Restored with Iran
events.description: Mediated by China, Saudi Arabia and Iran reached an agreement to restore diplomatic relations severed for seven years. This historic reconciliation shocked the world, demonstrating China's growing Middle East influence and Saudi foreign policy flexibility.

events.title: Syria Rejoins Arab League
events.description: Syria rejoined the Arab League after a 12-year suspension. Saudi Arabia played a key role in restoring Syria's status, marking a policy shift from isolating Assad to engagement.

events.title: Stance After Gaza War Erupts
events.description: After Hamas's attack on Israel triggered the Gaza War, Saudi Arabia suspended normalization talks with Israel. Saudi Arabia called for ceasefire and condemned Israeli actions, but avoided over-involvement, balancing relations with the US and domestic opinion.

events.title: Vision 2030 Progress Assessment
events.description: As 2030 approaches, Saudi Arabia assessed Vision progress. Though progress made in tourism, entertainment, and women's rights, economic diversification remains slow; oil still dominates. Human rights situation and political repression remain focal points of international criticism.

events.title: Renewable Energy Investment
events.description: Saudi Arabia heavily invested in solar and wind projects, aiming for 50% renewable energy generation by 2030. This green transition aims to reduce domestic oil consumption, freeing more oil for export, while demonstrating environmental responsibility.

events.title: Riyadh Expo Preparations
events.description: Saudi Arabia is conducting massive infrastructure construction for Riyadh Expo 2030. The expo is expected to attract 40 million visitors, becoming a global stage to showcase Saudi transformation. This is one of Vision 2030's core projects.
